segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for moving this to 10:30. I was still untangling the parent account and the two plant locations on our side, but I’ve got the quote in front of me now.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: No problem. We just need to confirm whether 42 seats gets us the onboarding package you mentioned, or if that starts at 50.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: At 42 seats, you’re at $18,900 annually, and I can include the standard onboarding: two admin sessions, one end-user webinar, and the data import checklist. The 50-seat tier adds the quarterly business review, but pricing goes to $21,600.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. Our CFO asked if the invoice can split 60% to operations and 40% to finance. Same contract, just separate cost centers.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes, that’s fine. I’ll put the cost center split in the order form. I’ve got to get the approval packet over before lunch, so if you send the finance contact right after this, I can keep the March 18 start date.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: March 18 works if security review is done by the 12th. They’ll ask about data residency and SSO. Is that in the standard terms?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: SSO is included. Data residency is US-only by default, so that should be straightforward. The contract term would be 12 months, net 30, auto-renewal with 60 days’ notice unless you want that struck.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Legal usually pushes for 30 days’ notice. Can you send the redline language today?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: I can send the base order form today, and I’ll ask deal desk on the 30-day notice. I’m boxed in from 3 to 4:30 getting the quarter-end entries cleaned up, but I can get you a clean version by 2:15.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That’s fine. Send it to me and copy Dana in procurement. If the number stays under $19,000, we don’t need board approval.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Got it: 42 seats, $18,900, split invoice 60/40, March 18 go-live, and procurement copied. I’ll send the order form and the security summary before 2:15.
